blocks.prompt: 8 (i) Consider the function \(f(x) = 3x - 5\). Determine the domain and range of \(f(x)\).
blocks.explanation:
\(f(x) = 3x - 5\) is a straight line (degree 1).
We must find its domain and range.
Plan: no root or fraction, so the domain is all reals; solve \(y = 3x - 5\) for \(x\) for the range.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 3x - 5\).
To find: domain and range.
Method: Check for roots or fractions; then show every \(y\) is an output.

Domain
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty, \infty)\]
Why: \(3x - 5\) can be worked out for every real \(x\).

Range
\[y = 3x - 5 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{y + 5}{3}\]
\[\text{Range } f = (-\infty, \infty)\]
Why: For every real \(y\) this \(x\) is real, so every \(y\) is an output.

Check
\[y = 1:\; x = 2,\ f(2) = 6 - 5 = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Why: A chosen output really comes out.

blocks.prompt: 8 (ii) Consider the function \(f(x) = 3x - 5\). Is the function \(f\) one-to-one? Justify your answer.
blocks.explanation:
One-to-one means: equal outputs come only from equal inputs.
We must prove (or disprove) this for \(f(x) = 3x - 5\).
Plan: start from \(f(x_1) = f(x_2)\) and show that \(x_1 = x_2\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 3x - 5\).
To find / prove: whether \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2\).
Method: The definition of one-to-one, used directly.

Suppose two outputs are equal
\[f(x_1) = f(x_2)\]
\[3x_1 - 5 = 3x_2 - 5\]
Why: Take any two inputs from the domain that give the same output.

Simplify
\[3x_1 = 3x_2\]
\[x_1 = x_2\]
Why: Add 5 to both sides, then divide by 3.

Conclusion
Why: Equal outputs force equal inputs, so two different inputs never share an output. (Example: \(f(1) = -2\), \(f(2) = 1\), different.)
blocks.final_answer: Yes, \(f\) is one-to-one, because \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2\) (equal outputs imply equal inputs).

blocks.prompt: 8 (iii) Consider the function \(f(x) = 3x - 5\). Is the function \(f\) onto if the co-domain is all real numbers? Explain.
blocks.explanation:
Onto means: every element of the co-domain is an output.
The co-domain here is all real numbers.
Plan: take any real \(y\), find an \(x\) with \(f(x) = y\), and check it.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 3x - 5\), co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\).
To find / prove: whether every \(y \in \mathbb{R}\) has a pre-image.
Method: Solve \(3x - 5 = y\) for \(x\) and check.

Find the input for any \(y\)
\[3x - 5 = y\]
\[x = \dfrac{y + 5}{3}\]
Why: For every real \(y\), this \(x\) is a real number in the domain.

Check that it works
\[f\left(\dfrac{y + 5}{3}\right) = 3 \cdot \dfrac{y + 5}{3} - 5\]
\[= y + 5 - 5 = y \;\checkmark\]
Why: The input really gives the output \(y\), so range = co-domain.
blocks.final_answer: Yes, \(f\) is onto \(\mathbb{R}\): every real \(y\) is the image of \(x = \frac{y + 5}{3}\). (With (ii), \(f\) is bijective.)
